title: Feature Scaling Comparison MicroSim
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Compare a histogram and its summary statistics before and after min-max, standard, robust, and log scaling to see which methods change only the numbers and which change the shape.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to explain how min-max, standard, robust, and log scaling each change the values and the shape of a distribution, and how outliers affect each method.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Side-by-side comparison of a distribution before and after a learner-chosen transformation
keyQuestions: Why do the bars look the same after min-max, standard, and robust scaling?
With outliers present, why is the middle 50% so narrow after min-max scaling?
Which method would you choose for incomes, and why?
commonMisconceptions: Standard scaling makes data normally distributed (it changes the mean and spread, not the shape).
Robust scaling removes outliers (the outliers stay in the data, but they barely affect the median and IQR used for scaling).
Scaling changes the relationships in the data (the three linear methods keep every value in the same relative position).
assessmentOpportunities: Students are shown an unlabeled before and after pair of histograms with their statistics and must name the scaling method used and give the evidence. They then recommend a method for a column with a few very large values and justify it.
